name: scroll-area
title: ScrollArea
description: Source-owned Solid scroll container with native overflow behavior, styled scrollbar hooks, and stable root/viewport/scrollbar/thumb/corner anatomy.

meta.api: Exports ScrollArea plus ScrollAreaRoot, ScrollAreaViewport, ScrollAreaScrollbar, ScrollAreaThumb, and ScrollAreaCorner. ScrollArea accepts orientation="vertical"|"horizontal"|"both" and viewportClass for common source-owned composition.
meta.behavior: The current UI item uses native browser scrolling in the viewport. Vertical, horizontal, and two-axis overflow are selected with the orientation prop. Custom scrollbar dragging, thumb sizing, wheel routing, and scroll state synchronization are explicitly deferred until Core ScrollArea is accepted.
meta.accessibility: The viewport remains an ordinary div with native overflow. Consumers should add aria-label, aria-labelledby, role=region, tabindex, or semantic containers only when the scrollable content needs an announced landmark or keyboard focus target. Decorative scrollbar/thumb/corner parts are aria-hidden and non-interactive.
meta.customization: Use data-scope="ui-scroll-area" and data-part hooks for root, viewport, scrollbar, thumb, and corner. The viewport includes native scrollbar CSS hooks for Firefox and WebKit; apps can replace those classes for dense panels, terminal logs, tables, inspectors, and split panes.
meta.usage: Use ScrollArea for bounded panels with natural document content: dense inspector rails, detail panels, terminal or console output, wide tables, and compact settings panes. Prefer native page scrolling for full-page documents and avoid nesting scroll regions unless the product surface is intentionally pane-based.

parity.coss: Maps to the Coss Scroll Area item as a bounded overflow container with styled native scrollbar treatment and root/viewport/scrollbar/thumb/corner anatomy.
parity.baseUi: Core/Base UI composition is deferred because Keystone Core does not yet ship ScrollArea. Once Core owns custom scrollbar behavior, this UI item should become a thin styled wrapper around Core root, viewport, scrollbar, thumb, and corner parts.
parity.kobalte: Kobalte does not provide a dedicated ScrollArea primitive to mirror. Keystone keeps this source-owned and native-first until intrinsic behavior exists in Core.
parity.shadcn: Matches shadcn-style source ownership and anatomy naming while intentionally avoiding Radix-style custom scrollbar behavior until Keystone Core owns that behavior.
